schemas.name: builder/backpressure
schemas.description: A backpressure coverage survey: what each criterion's proof is, how strong it is, and which sensor runs it.

schemas.name: builder/execution-log
schemas.description: An append-by-convention execution log: minted id, timestamp, free text, and zero or more addresses.

schemas.name: builder/fence
schemas.description: A dispatch fence: the paths a delegated agent may and may not touch, as DATA rather than prose. Each row carries its pattern, whether it allows or forbids, the owner who may change it, the cause it exists for, and an expiry — so a fence row cannot quietly outlive its reason, and an amendment is a row edit with an author rather than a paragraph appended to a brief. `harness plan fence` compares a change's touched paths against these rows and refuses out-of-fence work by naming both the path and the row that refused it.

schemas.name: builder/plan
schemas.description: A builder plan: goals, acceptance criteria, phases, tasks, and one assertion list per task. Assertion lists live in `done_when`, where `pressure` is MANDATORY (a backpressure row, or the literal `not-applicable`), and `tasks[].done` is target-pinned at it so a task's state is derived from assertions and can be derived from nothing else. The deprecated `evidence` alias was dropped in tk-7161 (plan 071, ph-7103) — the same commit that migrated the exemplar — after serving its one purpose: letting frozen corpora keep validating while they moved.

schemas.name: builder/review
schemas.description: A review round as a document: findings as addressed rows, and a verdict that links every one of them to what was decided about it. Review history is normally prose in a chat log — unqueryable, and gone the moment the window scrolls. As rows, 'which findings were refuted, and on what grounds' is a jq one-liner, across reviews and across models. Dim-0 rows record what happened when a reviewer mutated a control on purpose, and carry a `pressure` link to the fixture that fired — so 'the tests would have caught it' is a citation rather than a claim.

schemas.name: pij-team/impl-guide
schemas.description: An implementation guide (impl-suggestion): prime's architecture-level instruction to the pm on HOW this plan's work decomposes — the composable-service units, their interfaces, which can run in parallel, how they compose, and whether the pm codes solo or fans out to coders. Seeded from the pij-team skill's template, iterated by prime before the pm is spawned.

schemas.name: pij-team/packet
schemas.description: A pij-team handover packet: the document a seat (pm, coder, or reviewer) is dispatched with. One schema for all three roles — the role field selects which template seeded it. Copied from the pij-team skill's templates/ into the plan folder, edited via ddocs, then delivered by path pointer in the pij send.

schemas.name: pij-team/settings
schemas.description: Team settings held in government: the default model/harness per role (pm, coder, reviewer) that pij-team spawns use unless a plan's impl-guide overrides them. Single-writer: o-prime edits via ddocs; everyone else reads.

schemas.name: prd/requirements
schemas.description: A product requirements register: numbered requirements as rows, each with a completed state and provenance notes. Amendments edit the row and say so; rows are never deleted.

schemas.name: reconstruct/conversation
schemas.description: A reconstructed conversation: timestamped turns selected out of telemetry stores (git-ai metrics-db, omp native sessions, pij ledgers) by a YAML config. Generated by scratch/reconstruct/scripts/reconvo.py — regenerate rather than hand-edit rows.

schemas.name: reconstruct/spine
schemas.description: A semantic reconstruction spine: the phases and beats of an orchestrated build, each beat typed by mode (conversation / plan / straight / swarm) and kind (ask / ruling / architecture / dispatch / milestone / incident / release / retro), with evidence pointers. Authored from telemetry reconstruction; edit via ddocs or edit-json-then-build.
